events.body:
The driver cancelled this trip; the app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and his chat and statement say only that he waited and no rider appeared [F10][F11][F14]. No message or statement gives a reason of his own (no car trouble, no other job, no refusal), so NS-0 reads "met": the cancellation is assessed under NS-1, not NS-3 [F4][F14][NS-0].

On NS-1 the record is complete on its face. Arrival: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:44:40, 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 6 m [F7][F1] — NS-1(i) is met. Waiting: counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival, cancellation at 08:50:20 is 5 min 40 s after arrival, with 6 min 50 s cumulative within 200 m [F6][F2] — NS-1(ii) is met. Contact: 2 timestamped in-app messages (first 08:45:10) and 1 in-app call (08:46:10) before cancelling [F5][F13][F12] — NS-1(iii) is met. Continuous presence: stationary 40 m from the pickup 08:44:40–08:50:20 [F3][F7] — NS-1(iv) is met. All four conditions hold, so NS-2 does not void the $5.00 fee on record [F8][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-9 does not apply: the rider has no prior no-show in 30 days [F18], and both profiles show 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days, so no account flag is supportable [F18][F19][NS-9]. The profile facts are not used to decide anything [F18][F19].

The safety screen, however, is decisive. The complaint states that when the rider called back about the charge, the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked where I live", and that she "felt very uncomfortable" — on its face an allegation of harassment and inappropriate conduct aimed at the rider. That is a safety allegation under SAFE-1, screened whatever type was filed, and the court may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on it [SAFE-1][SAFE-3]. The only logged call is the driver's own unanswered call at 08:46 with no recording, and the chat holds only the driver's two messages, so no system record captures or rebuts the post-trip call the rider describes [F12][F13]. Because the screen is suspected, the case must go to a person, and the outcome cannot be a system ruling on the fee [SAFE-1].

Confidence: NS-1 is clear-cut on the records, but the escalation rests on the rider's uncorroborated account of a post-trip call, so the overall reading is moderately rather than fully clear.

ruling.recommended_action: Send case file to human review (safety escalation): rider's complaint alleges inappropriate sexual remarks and a question about where she lives, made in a post-trip call; no system record of that call exists and the driver has no recording to rebut it. Route the case to Trust & Safety under SAFE-1; assess interim measures under SAFE-4. Do not release or void the $5.00 no-show fee until the human reviewer decides; the NS-1 conditions are separately satisfied on the records. If the safety allegation is not upheld, the $5.00 fee stands under NS-1 with no driver flag (F18, F19).

rejected_claims.reason: The request to waive the fee on safety grounds cannot be granted or refused by the system: the post-trip comments alleged in the complaint are a SAFE-1/SAFE-3 matter and the case goes to a human instead of a fee ruling [F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-3]. On the fee itself, all four NS-1 conditions are met on the records [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F7].

The argument that the uncorroborated post-trip call defeats the safety ground fails: SAFE-1 screens the text of the complaint whatever the dispute type, and the absence of any recording of that call [F12][F13] is exactly what requires human review [SAFE-1].
TH-1 finality by amount does not apply here: a safety allegation routes the case to a person regardless of the $5.00 amount [F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-3], so the under-$10 system path is displaced.

The clean driver profile does not decide the case: the profile never decides a case alone [F18][F19], and it cannot answer the safety screen, which concerns the rider's complaint rather than the driver's history [SAFE-1]. NS-9 is correctly not triggered [F18].

The rider's own concession that the $5.00 fee is not voided under NS-2 is correct and is adopted: NS-1(i)–(iv) are satisfied on the records [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F7], and no NS-2 or NS-9 flag follows [F18][F19][NS-2].

The rider's account that he cancelled the moment she came out is contradicted by the timeline: cancellation was 5 min 40 s after arrival and 10 min 20 s after acceptance [F4][F6], and the fee stands under NS-1 [F8][NS-1].

element_findings.reason: The app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and the driver's own words state only that he waited more than five minutes and no rider appeared, then cancelled [F10][F11][F14]. No message or statement offers a reason of his own (car trouble, another job, a personal matter, refusal of the trip), so the cancellation is a rider no-show under NS-1 and NS-3 does not apply [NS-0].

No chat, call log or GPS record captures that call (the only logged call is the driver's unanswered 08:46 call with no recording) [F12][F13], so the safety allegation cannot be resolved on the records and SAFE-3 bars a system ruling on it.

what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, left before 5 minutes, or not both messaged and called the rider, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver did press arrival and was physically at the pickup point: his closest approach was 6 m at 08:44:35 and he was stationary 40 m from the pickup at (1.3324, 103.8493) from 08:44:40 to 08:50:20, so NS-1(i) and NS-1(iv) are satisfied on the GPS record.

The free wait ran from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival (08:44:40) and more than 5 minutes elapsed before cancellation at 08:50:20 (5 min 40 s after arrival; 6 min 50 s cumulative within 200 m), so the NS-1(ii) waiting threshold was met.

Before cancelling the driver sent 2 timestamped in-app messages (first 08:45:10) and made 1 in-app call (08:46:10, unanswered), meeting the NS-1(iii) contact requirement; the app reason was rider_no_show and his own words state only that no rider appeared, not a reason of his own.

Every NS-1 condition (i)–(iv) appears on the system records, so the $5.00 cancellation fee on record is upheld and NS-2 does not void it; no flag_account is supportable against the driver on this record.

The rider nevertheless asks the fee be waived: the complaint states the driver, when called back about the charge, made comments about her body and asked where she lives, and that she felt very uncomfortable — conduct alleged after the trip that no fare or GPS record contradicts, and which the court must screen under SAFE-1 (rider's account; driver's 0 upheld and rider's 0 disputes at F18/F19 do not decide it).

weaknesses: The no-show fee stands on the face of the records: F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F7 satisfy all four NS-1 conditions, so under NS-1/NS-2 the driver was entitled to cancel and charge, and the official no-show precedent DISP-002 upheld the fee.

The safety complaint rests only on the rider's own words in the complaint; there is no chat, call recording or other system record of the alleged post-trip comments (F12, F13), so if it is read as a bare statement it loses to the system records.
F18 (rider: 0 disputes in 90 d) supports her credibility only weakly and cannot itself decide the case.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled for rider no-show: the app reason is rider_no_show, his statement says he waited more than five minutes with no rider and then cancelled, and no message, statement or record gives any reason of his own (no car trouble, no other job, no refusal of the trip).
NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:44:40 while 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m radius, and his closest approach was 6 m.

NS-1(ii) is satisfied: the free wait ran from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (08:44:40) and the driver cancelled at 08:50:20, 5 min 40 s later — past the 5-minute free wait — having stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 6 min 50 s cumulatively and stationary 40 m from it from 08:44:40 to 08:50:20, so presence is proven throughout.
NS-1(iii) is satisfied: before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first at 08:45:10, "Reached, black Hyundai Ioniq, waiting at the pickup") and made 1 in-app call (08:46:10).

Every NS-1 condition holds on system records (GPS, timeline, chat), so under NS-1 the $5.00 no-show fee stands and is payable to the driver; the rider's assertion that he cancelled the moment she came out is contradicted by the timeline, which shows the cancellation 10 min 20 s after acceptance and 5 min 40 s after arrival.

The rider's account of comments about her body and asking where she lives, made in a call she placed after the trip, is not recorded anywhere in the chat, call log or GPS records for this trip; the only logged call is the driver's unanswered call at 08:46, so it is an untimestamped statement that no system record corroborates.
The driver's record supports no adverse add-on: 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days across 612 trips, so no NS-9 or RD-6 type flag applies and the profile facts cannot decide this case.
The disputed amount is $5.00, under $10, so the system ruling is final and no human review under TH-1 is required on the amount.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint alleges comments about her body and a question about where she lives, which on its face is a safety-relevant allegation of inappropriate conduct/harassment and may draw a SAFE-1 screen to human review regardless of the NS-1 finding; the driver has no recording disproving it.
F13 shows the driver's only call attempt at 08:46 was not answered and there is no recording, so the driver cannot rebut the content of the post-trip call the rider describes.

F6/F7 record arrival at 08:44:40, only 4 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:40:00 and 2 min 20 s after first entering the 200 m radius at 08:42:55 — the rider may argue the driver was early and that the wait should be counted from the scheduled pickup time, though NS-1(ii) uses the later of the two and the arrival-based count still exceeds 5 minutes.

The rider's message history is empty (F12 lists only the driver's 2 messages), so the driver cannot point to any rider reply confirming she was aware he was waiting; NS-1(iii) requires only the driver's message and call, which are recorded.

points.response: Conceded: the app reason (F4) and his own statement (F14) give no reason of his own, so NS-0:reason reads met and the cancellation is assessed under NS-1, not NS-3.
Conceded: F7 records the "I'm Here" tap at 08:44:40, 40 m from the pickup, and F1 puts his closest approach at 6 m, so NS-1(i) is met.

Conceded on the timing: counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (08:44:40), cancellation at 08:50:20 is 5 min 40 s later (F6), and he stayed within 200 m for 6 min 50 s and stationary 40 m away (F2, F3), so NS-1(ii) and (iv) are met.
Conceded: F5 and F13 record 2 in-app messages (first 08:45:10) and 1 in-app call (08:46:10) before the cancellation, so NS-1(iii) is met.

Part-conceded: all four NS-1 conditions hold on the records (F1–F3, F5, F6, F7), so the $5.00 fee is not voided under NS-2 and I no longer contest the no-show finding itself; the fee is now sought only on the safety ground in C5 (SAFE-1), which NS-1 does not answer.

This does not defeat C5: it is true no system record captures the post-trip call (F12, F13), but SAFE-1 screens the text of the complaint itself, whatever the type filed, and it is the only record of that call — the absence of a recording is precisely why SAFE-1 sends it to a person rather than to a system ruling.

Ceded only as to NS-9/RD-6: F19 shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so no repeat-violation flag applies; that does not touch the SAFE-1 screen, which is about the rider's complaint, not the driver's history.

The $5.00 is under $10 (F8), so TH-1 makes a system ruling final on the amount, but TH-2/SAFE-1 route a safety category to a person regardless of amount, and the rider's complaint alleges inappropriate conduct and a question about where she lives.

Conceded, and it is my own case: the GPS shows closest approach 6 m at 08:44:35, the "I'm Here" tap 40 m from pickup, and a stationary position 40 m away from 08:44:40 to 08:50:20, so NS-1(i) and (iv) hold.

Conceded in the driver's favour: counting from the later of scheduled pickup and recorded arrival (08:44:40), cancellation at 08:50:20 is 5 min 40 s later and 6 min 50 s cumulative within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) is met and the fee stands under NS-1.

Conceded: 2 timestamped messages (first 08:45:10) and 1 in-app call (08:46:10) satisfy NS-1(iii), and the driver's only stated reason is the rider's absence — no reason of his own appears anywhere in F10-F14, so NS-0 reads "met" and NS-3 does not apply.

Agreed as far as it goes: on F1-F8 every NS-1 condition is met, so the $5.00 fee is upheld and NS-2 does not void it; I add only that F19 (612 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 d) confirms no flag_account is supportable against the driver.

The post-trip comments are not corroborated by any system record — the only logged call is the driver's own unanswered call at 08:46 (F13) and the chat holds only his two messages (F12) — so on the record the fee is not waivable; but if the court reads the complaint's words (comments about her body, asking where she lives, "felt very uncomfortable") as an inappropriate-conduct allegation, SAFE-1 requires the case to go to a person, and the driver does not resist that screening.
